subject: Request: temporary coverage & hiring-freeze exception for Senior ML engineer
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary coverage & hiring-freeze exception for Senior ML engineer

Hi all,

Quick note — Priya (Sr. ML Engineer on the POC team for Acme) submitted a parental leave request starting Feb 1 for ~12 weeks. Her work is mission-critical for the next two checkpoints (model calibration + deployment automation). With the current hiring freeze, I need a short-term plan to avoid feature regressions for the Acme POC.

Options I evaluated (details in attached rotation_proposal_v2.xlsx):
- Short-term contractor (12 weeks) to cover inference infra and calibration (preferred) — est. $55k all-in.
- Internal rotation: move one mid-senior IC from infra (4 team) for 8–12 weeks — headcount neutral but needs manager sign-off and impacts delivery on infra roadmap.
- Stretch mode: split responsibilities across team — higher risk to timeline/quality.

Ask: can People Ops and Finance approve a hiring-freeze exception for a 12-week contractor OR sanction an internal rotation? I need decision by EOD Wed (2027-01-13) so hiring/procurement can move. Attached: parental_leave_request.pdf and the rotation plan with risks and cost.

If approved, next steps I suggest:
- Evelyn: confirm forms and exception criteria.
- Laura: approve the $55k contractor budget or propose alternative funding.
- Markus: sign off on technical gating and tradeoffs.

Thanks — I can hop on a quick sync if helpful.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary coverage & hiring-freeze exception for Senior ML engineer

Thanks for the clear summary, Dylan.

A few quick clarifying questions before we process an exception:
1) Exact leave dates (start/end) and whether Priya will be fully out or on partial schedule.
2) Is this headcount-neutral acceptable as contingency if we go with internal rotation?
3) Any regulatory or access needs (VPN, dataset access, customer IP) for an external contractor?

Operationally: People Ops can approve a time-limited exception for critical customer-facing work if Finance signs off on the spend and the hiring-freeze committee OKs it. If we go with a contractor, we need a signed parental leave form (attachment) and a short justification doc (I can template this).

I can start the exception request doc; please send the confirmed dates and mark the preferred option.

Evelyn Hart
Senior People Partner
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary coverage & hiring-freeze exception for Senior ML engineer

Dylan — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I ran preliminary numbers with Finance. Short answer: Finance can approve up to $60k for a 12-week contractor for critical customer-delivery work, provided the hiring-freeze exception is scoped and timeboxed in Confluence and the team tracks burn to the Acme POC cost center.

Notes:
- We need a cost-breakdown spreadsheet (I attached finance_cost_breakdown.xlsx) and a Confluence page link to the exception request before releasing funds.
- If you choose internal rotation, reassigning an IC requires the owning manager to confirm delivery adjustments; that is lower cash but higher schedule risk.

I'll provisionally greenlight the contractor spend; final release once Evelyn files the exception and assigns an approver from the hiring-freeze committee (Maria H.).

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary coverage & hiring-freeze exception for Senior ML engineer

Appreciate the proactive plan, Dylan. I am prepared to approve an exception on the following conditions:
1) Contractor must be vetted by Security (access control) and sign our standard NDA and data-handling addendum.
2) We clearly identify the three deliverables Priya would own during the 12-week window and a rollback plan if the contractor fails to deliver.
3) Product (PM) confirms this won't block any cross-team milestones — otherwise we prefer internal rotation.

If those are satisfied, you have my sign-off for the exception and the spend cap Laura outlined. Please loop in Security and the assigning PM.

-Markus
VP Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: elena.sosa@acme.com, tara.hr@talentbridge.com
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary coverage & hiring-freeze exception for Senior ML engineer

Thanks everyone — quick updates inline and attaching the signed parental_leave_request.pdf plus the updated rotation_proposal_v2.xlsx (now includes deliverables and rollback plan).

- Priya confirmed full parental leave from 2027-02-01 to 2027-04-25 (12 weeks). I attached her signed form.
- Preference: contractor for 12 weeks to preserve infra roadmap. I already had an initial convo with Tara at TalentBridge — Tara is ready to provide a pre-vetted candidate that meets our security checklist.
- Action items: Evelyn to file the exception request and route to Maria H. for final hiring-freeze committee sign-off; Laura to release funds once the Confluence exception is live; Markus to confirm tech gating (happy to provide a 30-min walkthrough of the three deliverables).

> 2) We clearly identify the three deliverables Priya would own during the 12-week window and a rollback plan if the contractor fails to deliver.
> 3) Product (PM) confirms this won't block any cross-team milestones — otherwise we prefer internal rotation.
>
> -Markus

I'll follow up with a short Confluence draft and loop in Security and PM. Thanks for the quick turn.

—Dylan

Redwood Inference
